cards.explanation: The answer is each one's own ability. Verse 15 says it plainly: “…each according to his own ability.” (Matthew 25:15) So five, two and one were not a lucky draw, friends. Nobody got a number pulled out of a hat. The master looked at each servant and handed over an amount to match.

The answer is five more talents. Verse 16 says he “…went at once and put them to work and gained five more.” (Matthew 25:16) Five he was given, five he gained. That puts him at ten talents total, and you'll hear that number again before the passage is over. He doubled what he had.

The answer is True. Verse 17 says, “Likewise, the one with the two talents gained two more.” (Matthew 25:17) Two in, two more out. That makes four, a full doubling, same as the first servant. Smaller pile, same result.

The answer is that he digs a hole and hides it. Verse 18 says he “…dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.” (Matthew 25:18) That's it, friends. That's the whole plan. The other two servants were out putting the money to work, and he was out digging a hole.

The answer is False. Verse 19 says, “After a long time the master of those servants returned…” (Matthew 25:19) He was gone a good while. Long enough that waiting got to be part of the job, and that goes for every servant.

The answer is “many.” Verse 21 says, “You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things.” (Matthew 25:21) A few things was the starting point. Many things is where it leads, bakers. The master doesn't hand this servant a little pat on the back.

The answer is that the master's reply is word for word the same. Put verse 21 next to verse 23 and they match exactly. Both servants hear, “Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!” (Matthew 25:21, 23) The two-talent servant had a smaller pile, and he got the very same words. The size of the pile didn't change the praise.

The answer is afraid. That's the word the servant uses in verse 25: “So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground.” (Matthew 25:25) Notice that's his own explanation, told to the master's face. Fear was the reason he gave for the hole.

The answer is False. The master is not pleased. His reply in verse 26 begins, “You wicked, lazy servant!” (Matthew 25:26) Keeping the money safe didn't win any praise from him, friends. Burying dough in a hole doesn't make it rise, and the master noticed.

The answer is that he should have deposited it with the bankers. Verse 27 says, “Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my return I would have received it back with interest.” (Matthew 25:27) The master names the bankers and the interest. It was a simple step, and the servant skipped it.

The answer is the one who has ten talents. Verse 28 says, “Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.” (Matthew 25:28) That's the servant who started with five and gained five more. The one talent goes to the servant who already has the biggest pile.

The answer is True, and it's a hard line. Verse 29 says, “But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” (Matthew 25:29) The master says it right after he explains the first half, that everyone who has will be given more. Both halves come from the same verse, bakers.

The answer is into the outer darkness. Verse 30 says, “And throw that worthless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.” (Matthew 25:30) I think this is a heavy part, friends, and it should be read slowly. It's where the master's words end.
